verdict.rationale: Bun's first-party audit docs show it reading the package list from bun.lock, sending it to the npm advisory endpoint and printing a report. They also document a severity filter (--audit-level) and an automatic fix mode that upgrades vulnerable packages, and the docs index lists audits as a package-manager feature. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the audit command, documented details on output formats/CI exit codes.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can audit installed dependencies for known vulnerabilities directly from the CLI

citations.quote: Bun reads the package list from `bun.lock` (no `node_modules` required), sends it to the npm advisory endpoint, and prints a report.
`--audit-level=<low|moderate|high|critical>` - Only report vulnerabilities at this severity or higher
Runs the audit, then upgrades each vulnerable package to the lowest non-vulnerable version that every dependent's range allows, and installs.
Package Manager: Fast installs, workspaces, overrides, and audits with `bun install`.
